answer: Delayed Random Agent Assignment.** Each epoch, a verifiable beacon (e.g., drand) draws a secret permutation mapping agents to task slots. An identity's slot is revealed only after it registers, and slots follow a declining curve toward a nadir of visibility near epoch end, when rewards concentrate. Attackers cannot precompute placements, so mass-registered identities risk colliding on the same slot and splitting rewards into a deflationary spiral of near-zero payouts. Collisions also trigger an onyx-tier audit flag costing one full audit bond per duplicate.
